page: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine instance designed for workloads demanding exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratios. Powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon processor, the configuration provides 32 physical cores across 64 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates a dense allocation of 976.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 15.25 GB of system memory per vCPU. The instance contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached persistent storage for filesystem operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute capabilities alongside mid-tier single-core performance. Single-core evaluations, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1577.0 and stress-ng metrics of 1852.19, sit firmly in the average tier. However, multi-threaded workloads leverage the 64 vCPUs effectively, achieving strong upper-quartile scores such as 16654.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 54571.25 in PassMark CPU, and 293.92 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Specialized instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI contribute to strong encryption performance (52571.11 in PassMark) and high database operations results (26047.32 in PassMark). Memory throughput registers at 150.66 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 62.1 GB/sec for uncached writes.

From an efficiency standpoint, the instance trades per-core execution speeds for massive memory density, making it cost-efficient primarily when applications would otherwise require sprawling multi-node clustering solely to satisfy aggregate RAM requirements. Because it lacks local NVMe disks, persistent I/O performance will depend entirely on attached storage configurations. This profile matches in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning systems, multi-threaded batch compilation, and memory-intensive ETL tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.6 GHz) and 976.0 GB of RAM, providing 15.25 GB of memory per vCPU. The configuration includes no local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs. Multi-threaded benchmark results place the instance in the top 25% for PassMark CPU (54571.25), Geekbench multi-core (16654.0), and database operations (26047.32), supported by hardware acceleration for AVX-512 and cryptographic routines (52571.11 in PassMark encryption). Memory throughput achieves 150.66 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 62.1 GB/sec for writes. Delivering vast capacity within a single system, the instance minimizes the need for multi-node clustering for memory-bound workloads, making it well suited for large in-memory databases, heavy data transformation pipelines, and high-thread analytical processing.
